hero.subtitle: Authorization Code Exchange for web and mobile — GitLab OAuth application setup, API reference, and frontend examples.

overview.title: Overview
overview.description: GitLab login is optional and controlled by GITLAB_AUTH_ENABLED. When disabled, GitLab endpoints return 503 Service Unavailable. JWTs are never placed in the redirect URL; the API issues a one-time exchangeCode (Redis, 60 seconds). The same POST /auth/exchange endpoint is shared with other social providers.
items: Profile fetched via GET https://gitlab.com/api/v4/user after token exchange
Scope read_user for basic profile and email
Same token response shape as POST /auth/login

console.title: GitLab Applications
console.description: Register a user-owned OAuth application in your GitLab profile. The Redirect URI must match GITLAB_CALLBACK_URL exactly. Enable the read_user scope so the API can load the signed-in profile and email.
steps: In the left sidebar, open Access → Applications
Give it a Name and set the Redirect URI to your API callback (e.g. http://localhost:3000/api/v1/auth/gitlab/callback)
Save the application, then copy Application ID and Secret into GITLAB_CLIENT_ID / GITLAB_CLIENT_SECRET
Keep GITLAB_CALLBACK_URL identical to the Redirect URI you registered (use Renew secret in GitLab if you need to rotate the secret later)

env.title: Environment variables
env.description: Loaded from .env via src/config/gitlab-oauth.config.ts (namespace gitlabOAuth on ConfigService). See .env.example.

roles.title: Default roles for new GitLab users
roles.description: New GitLab users receive roles: [] by default (same as password register). Set GITLAB_OAUTH_DEFAULT_ROLES in .env to a comma-separated list of Role values (e.g. user or user,manager). Existing users linked by email keep their current roles.

flow.title: Sequence
items: User consents on GitLab; browser hits GET /api/v1/auth/gitlab/callback
API calls GET https://gitlab.com/api/v4/user, upserts user, stores exchangeCode in Redis, redirects to redirect?code=...
Client POSTs { code } to /api/v1/auth/exchange and receives JWTs

start.title: 1. Start OAuth
start.description: Opens GitLab consent at https://gitlab.com/oauth/authorize. Query redirect must match a prefix in GITLAB_REDIRECT_ALLOWLIST (or omit to use the first allowlist entry). Scope: read_user.

callback.title: 2. Callback
callback.description: Handled by the API. Token exchange uses https://gitlab.com/oauth/token. Redirects to your app with ?code= (or &code= if the URL already has a query).

exchange.title: 3. Exchange code
exchange.description: Public endpoint shared with other social providers. Consumes the code (single use) and returns the same shape as login.

web.title: Frontend — Web (SPA)
web.description: Typical flow: button starts OAuth in the same window (or popup); a callback route on your frontend origin reads code from the query string and calls exchange.
notes: Add your frontend callback URL to GITLAB_REDIRECT_ALLOWLIST (e.g. http://localhost:5173/auth/callback)
GITLAB_CALLBACK_URL must point at the Nest API, not the SPA
Store accessToken / refreshToken securely (memory + httpOnly cookie patterns as you prefer)

mobile.title: Frontend — Mobile (deep link)
mobile.description: Use a custom scheme (or universal link) in the allowlist. After GitLab, the API redirects to myapp://success?code=.... The app opens, parses the code, and calls exchange.
notes: Register the scheme in the OS / Expo app.json
Exchange over HTTPS against your API base URL

security.title: Security notes
items: Redirect URLs must match GITLAB_REDIRECT_ALLOWLIST prefixes
Exchange codes are single-use and expire in 60 seconds (Redis)
Existing local users are linked by verified GitLab email (gitlabId set; roles unchanged)
GitLab-only users have password null — password login / change-password will fail until a password is set
Email is required from gitlab.com/api/v4/user; login fails if GitLab does not return an email (scope read_user)

userModel.title: User model
userModel.description: Postgres entity / interface fields used by GitLab login:
items: gitlabId — unique nullable GitLab user id (id from /api/v4/user)
isActive — set true for new GitLab users
